Scenario adaptation limited to the callback-stop-return-teardown smoke behavior. The pinned fixture boots a real one-port net_null EAL, invokes a callback that calls ff_dpdk_stop, then returns through its cleanup path; its body has no explicit datapath, callback-count, or EAL-cleanup-result assertions. Ker’s one-shot run-stop case verifies exactly one caller callback, real original-Linux IPv4/IPv6 TCP/UDP traffic, stop, acknowledged EAL-worker reaping, and zero owned buffers before return. The source comments describe a single coupled EAL-main-loop turn, but that internal scheduling is not an asserted result and is not implemented by Ker’s autonomous workers. This mapping does not claim EAL-lcore callback or coupled dispatch/RX/message/TX/accounting-loop equivalence; that broader architecture remains tracked separately under issue223.

Before accepting any secondary, the resident looks up every slot/generation/process/control-RX-TX-reply ring using original rte_ring_lookup and validates all128 actual objects, their capacity and SP/SC geometry. It also configures one original directional net_ring network port and its fixed epoch-independent RX/TX rings. Readiness reports actual128 lookups, one port and resident epoch/slot0. A real EAL secondary revalidates all128 objects, looks up the fixed queues and carries original imported-Linux IPv4/IPv6 TCP/UDP traffic. This adapts source TC-1 creation/lookup/network-port assertions, not source ring-name ABI or the complete reload dispatcher.

A real EAL secondary under a different plain master validates a nonzero epoch/slot, shared directory/pool and exact coordinate ring names. It attaches the resident-configured original net_ring PMD, obtains the sole journaled consumer grant and performs actual TX/RX bursts with exact frame bytes and original counter deltas. The primary only drains data after exact consumer death and never consumes network data while this borrower lives. The source uses an original null PMD and does not require a physical NIC or Linux packet delivery; those broader boundaries remain tracked separately.

A BUILD_TESTING-only source-shaped observer exercises the pinned two-masters/single-consumer scenario with two distinct live masters and real EAL secondaries sharing generation0/process0. Each worker independently samples stable no-hardware state and the same nonzero PMD owner epoch across a shared barrier; the primary is not owner. The resident holds one valid journaled probe mbuf in each distinct typed message ring simultaneously, then drains and verifies exactly one correctly owned token/reply per ring before either chain exits. This adapts only this source scenario's same-generation ownership and message-ring assertions. It does not qualify cross-generation dispatch/drain, general exception/KNI packet ownership, physical-device handover, queued packet crash/recovery, established-flow continuity or the full reload path.

Production epoch-status queries the resident exact-pidfd census. Distinct actual master/secondary epochs remain live while borrowers survive master death, including a frozen orphan. After exact borrower death and registration release their epochs become non-live while the resident epoch0 remains live. Reusing the old slot for a newer real secondary never revives the old epoch. This qualifies the source TC-4 liveness verdict, not its F-Stack heartbeat timeout implementation, drain-peer protocol or full reload flow.

The focused native EAL adapter sends an unseeded typed coordinate query only after the real secondary is authenticated and ATTACHED. The resident answers only for that live peer while its exact original control mbuf remains journaled; the worker uses only the returned live nonzero coordinate with the existing production ring_name helper to look up the proc-1 RX ring and prove it differs from slot-zero. The guest also rejects an unbound query with EPERM and no coordinate data, then proves exact worker/supervisor pidfd cleanup, 511-object baseline and DRAINED. This adapts the source test's coordinate-query/ring-name selection assertion only. It does not implement or claim FF_RELOAD_CMD_QUERY/ff_ipc wire compatibility, cookies, multi-candidate discovery, fallback semantics, TCP/flow migration or full reload.

The Ker resident authenticates an explicitly drain-authorized EAL secondary and accepts only its worker-origin heartbeat after the master exits. A second real EAL worker with a distinct epoch/slot but the same generation/process sees the fresh orphan as its peer; after that worker exits and the 2-second freshness window elapses, peer selection falls back to the caller epoch/opposite generation. The SHA-bound native guest run checks the source peer1=1/peer2=0 assertions, exact process cleanup and the 511-object pool baseline. This maps only this peer-liveness/drain-semantics case; DPDK drain-TX cases, flow-map, external packet TX, TCP continuity and full reload remain unqualified.

The exact A4 namespace-recycle scenario now uses one resident EAL primary, three plain masters and their real EAL secondaries. All three reusable slots are occupied; every master is killed without RELEASE while its worker remains alive, so slots and control leases remain protected. After all exact worker lifetimes end and original EAL cleanup completes, a fourth plain master and real secondary obtain an epoch greater than every abandoned epoch, a nonzero reusable slot, validated directory/ring/pool lookup and four real shared-mbuf probe roundtrips. No fallback to primary epoch/slot zero, unreaped processes or outstanding control objects is accepted. This qualifies namespace recycling only, not USR2 application orchestration, hardware handover or packet delivery.

Only the failing write return is injected; no successful TAP/PMD operation is mocked.

Architecture-specific source assertion: the child must inherit the exact opaque FreeBSD pcurthread pointer from its parent. Original Linux/LKL manages its own task context; Ker host pthread TLS is intentionally isolated. Architecture-specific F-Stack wrapper assertion: a void* start routine returns non-NULL, but ff_start_routine discards it and pthread_join writes NULL into a caller result slot. Pinned LKL thread_create takes void (*)(void*) and thread_join takes only a thread handle, so neither tested return/result slot exists. Do not fabricate a result-returning callback or count owned argument completion as equivalent. Exact disposition: docs/fstack-thread-contracts.md and issue231.
Fail the actual LKL thread-wrapper allocation: thread_create returns its zero failure sentinel, errno remains ENOMEM and the routine never runs; F-Stack uses -ff_ENOMEM instead.

Architecture-specific FreeBSD PCPU assertion: despite its name, the source body does not create a thread or inject allocation failure. It clears pcurthread/pcpup, then invokes the test-local ff_pcpu_get/PCPU_GET(curcpu) mirror and expects wrapped panic. Original Linux/LKL has no such FreeBSD TLS/accessor. Ker panic-abort tests do not execute this macro and are not equivalent. Exact disposition: docs/fstack-thread-contracts.md and issue231.

Asserts the FreeBSD mbuf head M_PKTHDR bit. Original Linux VMA/skb interfaces have no such mbuf field; a fabricated mbuf mirror would not qualify. Explicit incompatible source layout under issue232 (Linux buffer-ownership contracts remain under issue225), not a Ker pass.

Asserts the initial FreeBSD head m_pkthdr.len field, not zero-filled payload storage. Linux VMA buffers have no mbuf header/write cursor. Explicit incompatible source layout under issue232 (Linux buffer-ownership contracts remain under issue225), not a Ker pass.

Real ker_posix_buffer_alloc rejects signed negative lengths converted to size_t (-1 and INT_MIN) with NULL/EINVAL, preserving a live native mapping. This adapts allocation rejection through the Linux-native API, not ff_zc_mbuf_get ABI.
Source allocates an owned minimal mbuf chain for zero capacity; native buffer_alloc(0) intentionally rejects EINVAL. No equivalent owned empty-chain API. Contract decision remains under issue225.
No staged write-cursor/owned-head length API. Filling a VMA or delivering a datagram does not prove repeated writes accumulate a head length. Remains under issue225.
No staged write-cursor API. Send-range rejection occurs at a different phase and cannot substitute for source write-overflow rejection. Remains under issue225.
No staged write-cursor API. Rejecting NULL send payloads does not prove NULL input rejection during owned-chain writes. Remains under issue225.
No staged write-cursor/head-length API. Linux zero-byte UDP send is a real datagram with a completion ID, not this no-op write. Remains under issue225.

Source asserts per-mbuf m_len, m_next and head-length mutation. Actual multi-VMA Linux sendmsg proves scatter-gather delivery/completions, not a source owned-chain write cursor. Remains under issue225.

Real native SO_ZEROCOPY send/sendmsg/sendmmsg reject NULL nonempty payloads with EFAULT before GUP; no receiver data, completion or caller-byte mutation. Linux EFAULT intentionally replaces the source owned-chain EINVAL; this maps the rejection scenario, not errno/API equivalence.

Real MSG_ZEROCOPY send/sendmsg reject one mapped extent of INT_MAX+1 bytes with EFAULT before GUP; no data, completion or caller-byte mutation. Native allocations are limited to INT_MAX. This maps single-extent rejection, not the ff_zc ABI or an aggregate iovec INT_MAX limit.

Source owned-chain send rejects zero bytes; original Linux UDP permits an empty datagram and allocates a zerocopy completion ID. Preserve Linux semantics; no equivalent owned-chain rejection API. Contract decision remains under issue225.

Source asserts only that a non-NULL 16-byte argument passes its mirror validator. Actual registered 16-byte MSG_ZEROCOPY send reaches original Linux, delivers exact peer bytes and completes through original MSG_ERRQUEUE starting at ID zero. No claim of FreeBSD owned-chain handoff or end-to-end copy elimination.
